summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove product-specific statutory ceilings on primary industry research and marketing customs charges, allowing future rate changes to be made through regulations.
Regulated rates could not exceed recommendations from relevant industry bodies, with fallback research or marketing bodies required to consult charge payers before recommending rates.
It would sit alongside the rural research governance and excise levy bills, preserving existing operative charge rates while changing the machinery for future adjustments.
changes: Buffalo research charge recommendations would be required from a declared body or the relevant research corporation.
Obsolete research council and fund definitions would be removed from the honey charge schedule.
The horticultural products schedule would replace incorrect references to leviable products with chargeable products.
summary.affected: Primary industry charge payers, including relevant exporters and producers, industry representative bodies and research and marketing corporations are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Detailed changes in the rural R&D bill allowing statutory research and development corporations to undertake marketing alongside industry-owned ones, requiring funding agreements between government and statutory RDCs to be in place by 1 July 2014, and streamlining board appointments by limiting selection committees to five members serving up to three years.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of a companion bill removing maximum research, development and marketing levy rate caps from the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999, requiring any levy rate to be recommended by industry bodies after consulting levy payers.

speeches.speaker: Dick Adams
speeches.brief: Detailed the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill's changes across 10 acts affecting 15 research and development corporations, including new funding agreements required from July 2014 and streamlined board selection processes, and paid tribute to retiring committee colleague Alby Schultz.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill but argued New Zealand should contribute to Australian RDC marketing levies under the Closer Economic Relations agreement since its exporters benefit too, and lamented that the Tatura Research Institute, once a world leader in orchard trellis systems, now has virtually no research scientists left.
